title: improv·artist · biological (Eva Hesse)
mutation_directive: improv artist: biological via Eva Hesse

improv_extras.practice: latex, fiberglass, organic asymmetry; cellular hanging forms

v1.feedback: The Hesse connection lands in palette and droop — latex-beige monochrome with catenary strands reads as hanging installation. But the differential-growth ring is purely 2D (XZ plane, all verts converge to y≈0.8), so the 'viscera' are really a flat doily with a skirt; Hesse's forms had irregular 3D volume and asymmetric clustering. Let growth vary in Y per-vertex (random sag offsets, not uniform age-ramp) so strands emerge from an uneven membrane at multiple heights. The cellular interior noise is too subtle — add a second population of thicker, shorter fibers or bead-like clumps along strands to evoke the latex-drip / fiberglass-node texture that distinguishes Hesse from generic string art.

v2.feedback: The Hesse mapping is legit — catenary fibers, per-vertex sag asymmetry, latex-beige monochrome, and strand-vs-bead populations all trace back to her hanging latex/fiberglass pieces. Two refinements: the differential growth lives in the xz-plane with y as pure droop, so from the default camera the form reads as a flat ring with threads dangling — consider seeding multiple growth rings at staggered heights or letting the growth curve wander in 3D to give the piece volumetric presence closer to Hesse's spatial installations. Second, 35K strand particles with additive blending will saturate the membrane into a bright smear at full density — switch to normal blending or reduce strand alpha below 0.3 so individual threads and the fiberglass-node hierarchy stay visually distinct.
